definitions.explanation: The order or sequence of actions to accomplish something.

examples.japanese: {手順|てじゅん}に{従|したが}って{作業|さぎょう}する。
examples.english: To work according to the procedure.

examples.japanese: {登録|とうろく}の{手順|てじゅん}を{説明|せつめい}します。
examples.english: I will explain the registration procedure.

examples.japanese: {手順|てじゅん}を{間違|まちが}えると{失敗|しっぱい}する。
examples.english: If you get the steps wrong, you will fail.

notes:
{手順|てじゅん} emphasizes the ordered sequence of steps needed to accomplish a task. It focuses on "what comes first, what comes next" rather than the method itself.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {手順|てじゅん}を{踏|ふ}む: to follow the proper steps
- {手順|てじゅん}を{確認|かくにん}する: to confirm the procedure
- {手順|てじゅん}を{間違|まちが}える: to get the steps wrong
- {手順|てじゅん}{書|しょ}: procedure manual
- {手順|てじゅん}{通|どお}りに: according to procedure

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手続|てつづ}き: procedure involving paperwork or formalities (bureaucratic)
- {方法|ほうほう}: method (broader, how to do something)
- {順序|じゅんじょ}: order, sequence (more abstract)
- {段取|だんど}り: preparation and planning of steps (informal)

USAGE:
Commonly used in technical, workplace, and instructional contexts. {手順|てじゅん} implies that the order matters — skipping or rearranging steps leads to failure.
